evidence.note: Differential probe (uv run python) exercised FakeFs vs LocalFs (shutil.copy2/os.replace/shutil.move over a temp dir) on 7 cases. Before fix: 6 divergences confirmed (copy_file onto dir wrote a file AT the dir path instead of into it; copy_file/move to a missing parent silently succeeded vs FileNotFoundError; copy_file onto itself silent vs SameFileError; move(x,x) ValueError vs no-op; replace_path of a dir FileNotFoundError vs rename; replace_path of a file over a dir silent vs IsADirectoryError). After fix all 7 match (SameFileError is an OSError subclass). Verdict CONFIRMED.

r-adapters (Fs port single adapter; FakeFs stays a FakeFs) and r-gemini-key-load (export GEMINI_API_KEY before review) read and applied; the change stays inside the claimed globs ddflow/adapters/fakes/fs.py + tests/test_adapter_fs.py; no hub file edited (r-extension-contract).

evidence.note: Fixed ddflow/adapters/fakes/fs.py (copy_file/move/replace_path now mirror LocalFs) + regression tests in tests/test_adapter_fs.py. Differential probe confirms FakeFs matches shutil.copy2/os.replace/shutil.move on all 7 named cases.

chunk_findings.detail: When `src` is a directory and `dst` is an existing file, `replace_path` does not reject the operation. Given `self.files = {"f": ...}` and `self.dirs = {"dir"}`, `replace_path("dir", "f")` returns successfully. `_relocate_dir("dir", "f")` executes `self.dirs.add("f")` while `self.files["f"]` remains, leaving `"f"` as both a file and a directory. Real `os.replace` raises `OSError` (NotADirectoryError on POSIX) and leaves the filesystem unchanged.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/fs.py:replace_path

chunk_findings.detail: `replace_path` does not have the containment guard that `move` has, so a directory can be “renamed” onto a path inside itself. With `self.dirs = {"a", "a/b"}` where `"a/b"` is empty, `replace_path("a", "a/b")` succeeds and ends with `self.dirs == {"a/b"}`. Real `os.replace("a", "a/b")` raises `OSError` (invalid argument); the fake silently changes the directory tree incorrectly.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/fs.py:replace_path

chunk_findings.detail: The new `_require_parent(d)` check is after `if d.startswith(s + "/"): raise ValueError`. For a missing parent under the source directory, e.g. `move("a", "a/missing/file")` with `"a"` an existing directory and `"a/missing"` absent, the method still raises `ValueError`, not the promised `FileNotFoundError`. The missing-parent fix is therefore unreachable for this class of missing-parent input.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/fs.py:move

chunk_findings.detail: `copy_file` only tests `self.is_dir(d)` before appending the source basename, not after. If `d` is an existing directory that itself contains a directory at the joined target, e.g. `copy_file("f", "dir")` when `self.dirs` contains `"dir/f"`, the code falls through to `self.files[d] = self.files[s]`. That makes `"dir/f"` exist in both `self.dirs` and `self.files`. Real `shutil.copy2` would raise `IsADirectoryError`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/fs.py:copy_file

chunk_findings.detail: The regression for `copy_file("/f", "/f")` uses `pytest.raises(OSError)`, but the LocalFs contract called out in the intent and in the test comment is specifically `shutil.SameFileError`. Any other `OSError` raised for any reason would also satisfy this assertion, so an implementation can still diverge from LocalFs on the exception type and the test will pass. It should assert `pytest.raises(shutil.SameFileError)` or otherwise verify the caught type.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_adapter_fs.py:test_fake_copy_file_mirrors_local_on_directories_and_parents

chunk_findings.detail: The directory-rename regression checks `f.files == {"/renamed/f": b"1"}` and `not f.is_dir("/dir")`, but never checks `f.is_dir("/renamed")`. An implementation that only rewrites child file paths from `/dir/...` to `/renamed/...` without recording `/renamed` as a directory would still pass the test, even though FakeFs would still diverge from LocalFs for subsequent `is_dir("/renamed")` checks.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_adapter_fs.py:test_fake_replace_path_mirrors_local_on_directories

chunk_findings.detail: `copy_file` of a path onto itself raises a bare `OSError`, not `shutil.SameFileError`. Given `FakeFs({"/f": b"1"}).copy_file("/f", "/f")`, a caller that catches `shutil.SameFileError` (what LocalFs/`shutil.copy2` actually raises, and what bug B-fakefs-diverges-from-localfs names) still diverges. `test_fake_copy_file_mirrors_local_on_directories_and_parents` only asserts `pytest.raises(OSError)` and never runs LocalFs, so it stays green for the wrong type.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/fs.py:copy_file

chunk_findings.detail: Replacing a directory onto an existing file succeeds and leaves both a file and a directory at the destination. Given `FakeFs({"/file": b"x"})` plus `mkdir("/dir")` then `replace_path("/dir", "/file")`, the file branch is skipped, `_under("/file")` and `_dirs_under("/file")` are empty, and `_relocate_dir` never pops `self.files["/file"]`. Real `os.replace` of a directory over a non-directory fails (`NotADirectoryError`/`ENOTDIR`) and does not clobber. The new tests never pass a file as `dst`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/fs.py:replace_path

chunk_findings.detail: `replace_path` of a directory into its own descendant is not rejected (unlike `move`, which checks `d.startswith(s + "/")`). Given `FakeFs({"/a/f": b"1"}).replace_path("/a", "/a/child")`, the non-empty check looks only under `/a/child`, the parent `/a` exists, and `_relocate_dir` rewrites `/a/f` to `/a/child/f` while dropping `/a`. Real `os.replace` fails with `EINVAL` and leaves the tree unchanged.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/fs.py:replace_path

chunk_findings.detail: The descendant-rename regression uses a bare `with pytest.raises(OSError)` for `replace_path("/a", "/a/child")`. Since every filesystem error type (`FileNotFoundError`, `NotADirectoryError`, `IsADirectoryError`) is an `OSError` subclass, an implementation that raises `FileNotFoundError` here still passes the test, but `os.replace("/a", "/a/child")` raises a plain `OSError` (`EINVAL`). The test therefore does not pin the specific LocalFs exception the fix is supposed to match.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_adapter_fs.py:test_fake_replace_path_mirrors_local_on_directories

chunk_findings.detail: `_require_parent` treats “parent is an existing file” as a missing parent and raises `FileNotFoundError`. Given `FakeFs({"/f": b"1", "/p": b"x"}).copy_file("/f", "/p/child")` (same for `move` and `replace_path`), the helper’s `not self.is_dir("/p")` is true, so it raises `FileNotFoundError("/p")`. `shutil.copy2`, `shutil.move`, and `os.replace` all raise `NotADirectoryError` and leave the tree unchanged. The new tests only pass a wholly absent parent (`/no/parent/f`), so they stay green for this divergence.

chunk_findings.detail: `FakeFs.move('/a', '/a')` for an existing directory `/a` now enters `if self.is_dir(d)` and the newly added `if d == s: return`, so it silently returns as a no-op. Real `shutil.move('/a', '/a')` is not a no-op for a directory: `shutil.move` first sees that destination is an existing directory and resolves the target to `/a/a`, then raises an error because the directory cannot be moved into itself. The “no-op” case is valid only for files.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/fs.py:move

chunk_findings.detail: `_require_parent` only inspects the immediate parent string. With `FakeFs({"/p": b"content", "/src": b"s"})`, `copy_file('/src', '/p/sub/child')` (and similarly `move`/`replace_path`) has immediate parent `/p/sub`, which is not in `self.files`, so the helper raises `FileNotFoundError('/p/sub')`. But the real operations on a path where an intermediate component `/p` is an existing file raise `NotADirectoryError`, because path traversal hits a file before the missing component.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/fs.py:_require_parent

chunk_findings.detail: Given a tree where `/` is a directory and `/f` is an existing file, `replace_path('/', '/new')` enters the new directory branch (`s not in self.files` but `is_dir('/')` is true) and calls `_relocate_dir('/', '/new')`. `_relocate_dir` assumes a non-root source directory: for file `/f`, `d + f[len('/'):]` becomes `'/new' + 'f'` = `/newf`, not `/new/f`. The operation also succeeds where `os.replace('/', '/new')` raises `OSError` (the root cannot be renamed), so the new directory support corrupts the FakeFs mapping rather than mirroring LocalFs.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/fs.py:replace_path

Given a file `/f`, `FakeFs.move("/f", "/f/child")` reaches this guard and raises `ValueError`; real `shutil.move("/f", "/f/child")` raises `NotADirectoryError` because `/f` is a file, not a directory. chunk_findings.detail: The new descendant guard runs before `_require_parent(d)`, so it mishandles a missing destination that is textually under the source. With source directory `/a` and destination `/a/missing/child`, where `/a/missing` does not exist, the code raises a bare `OSError`. Real `os.replace("/a", "/a/missing/child")` raises `FileNotFoundError` (ENOENT) because the missing parent is encountered before any “directory into itself” OS error. The parent check must run first, or the descendant guard must only trigger once `d` actually resolves as a descendant.

chunk_findings.detail: When `FakeFs.move("/a", "/a/b")` is asked to move a directory into its own subtree, the changed guard now applies only to directories and raises `ValueError(f"cannot move {s} into itself ({d})")`. Real local filesystem behavior is not `ValueError`: `shutil.move('/a', '/a/b')` raises `shutil.Error`/`OSError` (`shutil.Error` is an OSError subclass), because a rename of a directory into itself is an OS-level invalid argument error. File-source descendant case was fixed, but this directory case still diverges from LocalFs.

chunk_findings.detail: The new `_require_parent(d)` call runs before the code decides whether the source is a file or a directory, so it now rejects directory moves to a missing parent. Given `FakeFs` containing a directory `/a` and no `/missing`, `FakeFs.move("/a", "/missing/a")` now raises `FileNotFoundError('/missing')`. Real `shutil.move("/a", "/missing/a")` succeeds in this situation: after `os.rename` fails, `shutil.move` sees the source is a directory and falls back to `copytree`, which creates `/missing/a`. This is a new divergence from `LocalFs` and contradicts the diff’s own comment that `move` should behave like `shutil.move`. The parent check should be limited to file sources; otherwise the fix corrects file moves but makes directory moves wrong.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/fs.py:move: `self._require_parent(d)`

chunk_findings.detail: The new self-subtree guard `if d.startswith(s + "/"):` is placed after `if d in self.files: raise NotADirectoryError(d)`, so it is unreachable when the destination is an existing file under the source directory. Input: `/a` is a directory and `/a/f` is an existing file. `FakeFs.replace_path("/a", "/a/f")` raises `NotADirectoryError` from the file check before the descendant check. Real `os.replace("/a", "/a/f")` raises `OSError` (`EINVAL`; `oldpath` is an ancestor of `newpath`), not `NotADirectoryError`. The replace self-subtree support still diverges for this input. The descendant check must happen before the existing-file check for directory sources.

evidence.budget_forced: all round-6 findings fixed; one clean re-verification

chunk_findings.detail: `_relocate_dir` adds `d` and the relocated descendant directories to `self.dirs`, but it never creates the missing ancestor directories of `d`. Real `shutil.move` handles a directory move to a missing parent through the `copytree` fallback, whose `os.makedirs` creates all missing parent components. For example, given `FakeFs` with `/a` a directory and `/a/f` a file, `FakeFs.move("/a", "/missing/a")` returns and adds `/missing/a` to `dirs` but does not add `/missing`. The moved directory is then unusable as a normal directory: `FakeFs.copy_file("/f", "/missing/a/f2")` raises `FileNotFoundError("/missing")` from `_require_parent`, even though LocalFs creates `/missing` during the move.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/fs.py:_relocate_dir

chunk_findings.detail: The descendant guard `if d.startswith(s + "/"):` runs before `_require_parent(d)`. Given a FakeFs containing directory `/a` and no `/a/missing`, `FakeFs.replace_path("/a", "/a/missing/child")` raises a bare `OSError` because the lexical descendant check fires first. Real `os.replace("/a", "/a/missing/child")` raises `FileNotFoundError`: the OS resolves the new path's parent `/a/missing` first and returns ENOENT; the EINVAL self-subtree error only applies when that parent can be resolved. This is the reverse of the move fix—`shutil.move` has its own `_destinsrc` precheck, but `os.replace` does not.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/fs.py:replace_path

chunk_findings.detail: The previously confirmed divergence `FakeFs.move("/a", "/missing/a")` (directory source to a missing non-descendant parent) is still absent from this regression test. The test covers a file source with a missing parent, `move(x, x)`, and `/a -> /a/b`, but not the directory-source missing-parent case the fix specifically changed. If the code regressed to call `_require_parent` again before deciding the source type, this suite would stay green. Add an assertion that moving `/a` with a file to `/missing/a` succeeds and places the file at `/missing/a/f`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_adapter_fs.py:test_fake_move_mirrors_local_on_parents_and_self

chunk_findings.detail: `replace_path` checks `if self._under(d) or self._dirs_under(d):` to reject replacing a non-empty directory, but on a real filesystem `os.replace` (or POSIX `rename`) successfully overwrites/replaces *existing* empty or non-empty directories depending on the platform/os rules, or raises `OSError` (`ENOTEMPTY` or `EEXIST`). In `FakeFs`, if `d` is an existing directory containing files (so `self._under(d)` is true), `replace_path` raises `OSError` even if `d` is a valid target directory that `os.replace` would replace. Given `FakeFs` with directory `/old` containing `/old/f` and directory `/new` containing `/new/g`, `FakeFs.replace_path("/old", "/new")` raises `OSError` ("cannot replace the non-empty directory '/new'") whereas real `os.replace("/old", "/new")` succeeds on POSIX when replacing an existing directory with another directory.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/fs.py:173

chunk_findings.detail: Directory `move` neither creates missing parents nor rejects a parent that is a file, despite the comment that a missing parent is created like `shutil.move`'s `copytree`/`os.makedirs` fallback. `_relocate_dir` only inserts `d` into `self.dirs`. Given a directory `/a` (and file `/a/f`) and no `/missing`, `move("/a", "/missing/a")` leaves `/missing` out of `self.dirs`, so a later `is_dir("/missing")` is false and `_require_parent` on a child of the moved tree raises `FileNotFoundError("/missing")` while the real tree has that parent. Given a file `/f` and directory `/a`, `move("/a", "/f/a")` also skips any parent check and records `/f/a` as a directory under a file; `shutil.move` fails (`os.rename` then `makedirs`) with `NotADirectoryError`/`FileExistsError`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/fs.py:_relocate_dir

chunk_findings.detail: The new descendant case calls `replace_path("/a", "/a/child")` where `/a/child` is not an existing file (`FakeFs` only has `/a/f`). That does not lock the confirmed divergence: given `/a` a directory and `/a/f` an existing file, `replace_path("/a", "/a/f")` must raise a bare `OSError` (EINVAL), not `NotADirectoryError` from a `d in self.files` check that runs before the subtree guard. A regression that restores that order leaves this suite green.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_adapter_fs.py:test_fake_replace_path_mirrors_local_on_directories

chunk_findings.detail: `pytest.raises(OSError)` on `move("/a", "/a/b")` does not lock the confirmed missing-intermediate case. Parent of `/a/b` is `/a`, which exists, so a parent check never fires. Given a directory `/a` and `move("/a", "/a/missing/new")`, checking `_require_parent` before the into-itself guard raises `FileNotFoundError("/a/missing")`. `shutil.move` raises `shutil.Error` (directory into itself) without requiring `/a/missing`. `FileNotFoundError` is an `OSError`, so even pointing this assertion at that input would still pass. The suite also never asserts the confirmed success path `move("/a", "/missing/a")` (missing non-descendant parent must relocate, not raise).
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_adapter_fs.py:test_fake_move_mirrors_local_on_parents_and_self

Given a directory `/a` (and file `/a/f`) and no `/missing`, `move("/a", "/missing/a")` leaves `/missing` out of `self.dirs`, so a later `is_dir("/missing")` is false and `_require_parent` on a child of the moved tree raises `FileNotFoundError("/missing")` while the real tree has that parent. Given a file `/f` and directory `/a`, `move("/a", "/f/a")` also skips any parent check and records `/f/a` as a directory under a file; `shutil.move` fails (`os.rename` then `makedirs`) with `NotADirectoryError`/`FileExistsError`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/fs.py:_relocate_dir

chunk_findings.detail: The new descendant case calls `replace_path("/a", "/a/child")` where `/a/child` is not an existing file (`FakeFs` only has `/a/f`). That does not lock the confirmed divergence: given `/a` a directory and `/a/f` an existing file, `replace_path("/a", "/a/f")` must raise a bare `OSError` (EINVAL), not `NotADirectoryError` from a `d in self.files` check that runs before the subtree guard. A regression that restores that order leaves this suite green.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_adapter_fs.py:test_fake_replace_path_mirrors_local_on_directories

chunk_findings.detail: `pytest.raises(OSError)` on `move("/a", "/a/b")` does not lock the confirmed missing-intermediate case. Parent of `/a/b` is `/a`, which exists, so a parent check never fires. Given a directory `/a` and `move("/a", "/a/missing/new")`, checking `_require_parent` before the into-itself guard raises `FileNotFoundError("/a/missing")`. `shutil.move` raises `shutil.Error` (directory into itself) without requiring `/a/missing`. `FileNotFoundError` is an `OSError`, so even pointing this assertion at that input would still pass. The suite also never asserts the confirmed success path `move("/a", "/missing/a")` (missing non-descendant parent must relocate, not raise).
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_adapter_fs.py:test_fake_move_mirrors_local_on_parents_and_self
